Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/762/3491179/ Remarks These glitches came from the Photon calibrator Pcal tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk subsystem specifically the one at Livingston's Y end The ultimate culprit turned out to be a radio frequency cable connection tab When the LLO PcalY is operating properly it shines two additional laser beams onto the Y end test mass symmetrically aimed above and below the midpoint These beams are modulated with among other things a Hz sine wave The extra light pressure from a mere watts of near infrared light suffices to jiggle the test mass just enough to be able to detect the Hz sine wave on the output side of the interferometer and from this one can figure out the exact ratio between very very small test mass movements and measurable variations in the photodiode current On Sun UTC still Sat local time after recovering from a lockloss amidst inclement weather the operators noticed a serious excess of low frequency noise along with indications that PcalY was acting up As a quick interim fix its responsibilities were moved over to PcalX Suspicions initially centered on the driver electronics for the AOM https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/762/3491179/ Remarks These glitches came from the Photon calibrator Pcal tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk subsystem specifically the one at Livingston's Y end The ultimate culprit turned out to be a radio frequency cable connection tab When the LLO PcalY is operating properly it shines two additional laser beams onto the Y end test mass symmetrically aimed above and below the midpoint These beams are modulated with among other things a Hz sine wave The extra light pressure from a mere watts of near infrared light suffices to jiggle the test mass just enough to be able to detect the Hz sine wave on the output side of the interferometer and from this one can figure out the exact ratio between very very small test mass movements and measurable variations in the photodiode current On Sun UTC still Sat local time after recovering from a lockloss amidst inclement weather the operators noticed a serious excess of low frequency noise along with indications that PcalY was acting up As a quick interim fix its responsibilities were moved over to PcalX Suspicions initially centered on the driver electronics for the AOM https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/762/3491179/ Remarks These glitches came from the Photon calibrator Pcal tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk subsystem specifically the one at Livingston's Y end The ultimate culprit turned out to be a radio frequency cable connection tab When the LLO PcalY is operating properly it shines two additional laser beams onto the Y end test mass symmetrically aimed above and below the midpoint These beams are modulated with among other things a Hz sine wave The extra light pressure from a mere watts of near infrared light suffices to jiggle the test mass just enough to be able to detect the Hz sine wave on the output side of the interferometer and from this one can figure out the exact ratio between very very small test mass movements and measurable variations in the photodiode current On Sun UTC still Sat local time after recovering from a lockloss amidst inclement weather the operators noticed a serious excess of low frequency noise along with indications that PcalY was acting up As a quick interim fix its responsibilities were moved over to PcalX Suspicions initially centered on the driver electronics for the AOM tab For the long story see LLO tab Much of the noise happened while LLO was not Observing The relevant times during which it was capable of producing Gravity Spy subjects are 18T UTC corroborated by spots in their proper places on all four test masses It's quite possible that the Crown glitches came from the Y end Since micro seismic ground motion happens at its own pace at each of the corner station and the two end stations several km away the motions of the test mass suspensions or better the motions of the vacuum chambers around each test mass and everything attached to the chamber walls are independent Seismic activity may be elevated in all three locations but any resulting glitches could well be interleaved like they are here test mass symmetrically aimed above and below the midpoint These beams are modulated with among other things a Hz sine wave The extra light pressure from a mere watts of near infrared light suffices to jiggle the test mass just enough to be able to detect the Hz sine wave on the output side of the interferometer and from this one can figure out the exact ratio between very very small test mass https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/762/3491179/ Remarks These glitches came from the Photon calibrator Pcal tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk subsystem specifically the one at Livingston's Y end The ultimate culprit turned out to be a radio frequency cable connection tab When the LLO PcalY is operating properly it shines two additional laser beams onto the Y end test mass symmetrically aimed above and below the midpoint These beams are modulated with among other things a Hz sine wave The extra light pressure from a mere watts of near infrared light suffices to jiggle the test mass just enough to be able to detect the Hz sine wave on the output side of the interferometer and from this one can figure out the exact ratio between very very small test mass movements and measurable variations in the photodiode current On Sun UTC still Sat local time after recovering from a lockloss amidst inclement weather the operators noticed a serious excess of low frequency noise along with indications that PcalY was acting up As a quick interim fix its responsibilities were moved over to PcalX Suspicions initially centered on the driver electronics for the AOM https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/762/3491179/ Remarks These glitches came from the Photon calibrator Pcal tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk subsystem specifically the one at Livingston's Y end The ultimate culprit turned out to be a radio frequency cable connection tab When the LLO PcalY is operating properly it shines two additional laser beams onto the Y end test mass symmetrically aimed above and below the midpoint These beams are modulated with among other things a Hz sine wave The extra light pressure from a mere watts of near infrared light suffices to jiggle the test mass just enough to be able to detect the Hz sine wave on the output side of the interferometer and from this one can figure out the exact ratio between very very small test mass movements and measurable variations in the photodiode current On Sun UTC still Sat local time after recovering from a lockloss amidst inclement weather the operators noticed a serious excess of low frequency noise along with indications that PcalY was acting up As a quick interim fix its responsibilities were moved over to PcalX Suspicions initially centered on the driver electronics for the AOM tab For the long story see LLO tab Much of the noise happened while LLO was not Observing The relevant times during which it was capable of producing Gravity Spy subjects are 18T UTC corroborated by the detector status summary page tab near UTC plus possibly brief ones about an hour earlier a few times during up to minutes each time around circa UTC There seems to have been an isolated precursor https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/762/3491179/ Remarks These glitches came from the Photon calibrator Pcal tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk subsystem specifically the one at Livingston's Y end The ultimate culprit turned out to be a radio frequency cable connection tab When the LLO PcalY is operating properly it shines two additional laser beams onto the Y end test mass symmetrically aimed above and below the midpoint These beams are modulated with among other things a Hz sine wave The extra light pressure from a mere watts of near infrared light suffices to jiggle the test mass just enough to be able to detect the Hz sine wave on the output side of the interferometer and from this one can figure out the exact ratio between very very small test mass movements and measurable variations in the photodiode current On Sun UTC still Sat local time after recovering from a lockloss amidst inclement weather the operators noticed a serious excess of low frequency noise along with indications that PcalY was acting up As a quick interim fix its responsibilities were moved over to PcalX Suspicions initially centered on the driver electronics for the AOM Either NOTA or Extremely Loud will be fine in such cases What happened is the glitch detection software known as "Omicron" works on minute long chunks of data at a time When there's a loud glitch near the end of one chunk Omicron may trigger once again on its outskirts at the beginning of the next chunk and we'll end up with two subjects from the same event one where it appears properly centered and another where it shows up left of center like here possibly processed with different rendering choices In the other direction it can also happen when there's a loud glitch near the beginning of a chunk then we'll get an extra subject with the glitch right of center https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3396143/ These medium frequency rippling glitches looking a bit like a river seen from the side on this occasion with most of the noise at Hz are a proposed glitch class of their own tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk thus for now best classified as NOTA They are not related to the spectral line at Hz coming from the mains power They were common at Hanford for a number of months starting in mid July and have become rare again now during O4b the second half of the fourth observing run https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3488580/ I saw two ovals at the bottom https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3489045/ This is a rather loud form of Scattered Light common at Livingston nowadays and not known from Hanford https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3488596/ None Of The Above These were a new kind of glitch tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 3314162?comment when they started happening at Livingston on a few had actually happened the day before they kept happening for a week until the cause was found and fixed https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3488909/ Well observed! "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN There's such a wide variety of glitches that a single way of turning them into images would not suffice Some are very tall and slender of short duration but spanning a broad band of frequencies Others are the opposite of long duration but limited to a few frequencies or just one Some are in between Our image production tries not always successfully to adapt to the shape of the glitch One and the same glitch can end up looking quite different depending on how it has been processed ! 4s around Q See also a list of Examples of common glitches at uncommon Q values tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk in our Talk pages snap > linking to the thread Apropos of this Any large size images inlined in the Field Guide should be pre scaled down from their original sizes to avoid having to load a half Megabyte image file only for the browser having to scale it down The thumbnail zooniverse org facility will do this nicely For examples the four images I just inlined here with links to their much larger originals have been pre scaled to pixels width by interposing thumbnails zooniverse org 300x into the URLs The whole shebang looks like this in the markdown input no line breaks no spaces except in the alt texts all in one single long line ! 4s around Q https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/730/3493090/ fuzzy range https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3494152/

"None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN There's such a wide variety of glitches that a single way of turning them into images would not suffice Some are very tall and slender of short duration but spanning a broad band of frequencies Others are the opposite of long duration but limited to a few frequencies or just one Some are in between Our image production tries not always successfully to adapt to the shape of the glitch One and the same glitch can end up looking quite different depending on how it has been processed ! 4s around Q See also a list of Examples of common glitches at uncommon Q values tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk in our Talk pages snap > linking to the thread Apropos of this Any large size images inlined in the Field Guide should be pre scaled down from their original sizes to avoid having to load a half Megabyte image file only for the browser having to scale it down The thumbnail zooniverse org facility will do this nicely For examples the four images I just inlined here with links to their much larger originals have been pre scaled to pixels width by interposing thumbnails zooniverse org 300x into the URLs The whole shebang looks like this in the markdown input no line breaks no spaces except in the alt texts all in one single long line ! 4s around Q https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/730/3493090/ fuzzy range https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3494152/

"None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN There's such a wide variety of glitches that a single way of turning them into images would not suffice Some are very tall and slender of short duration but spanning a broad band of frequencies Others are the opposite of long duration but limited to a few frequencies or just one Some are in between Our image production tries not always successfully to adapt to the shape of the glitch One and the same glitch can end up looking quite different depending on how it has been processed ! 4s around Q See also a list of Examples of common glitches at uncommon Q values tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk in our Talk pages snap > linking to the thread Apropos of this Any large size images inlined in the Field Guide should be pre scaled down from their original sizes to avoid having to load a half Megabyte image file only for the browser having to scale it down The thumbnail zooniverse org facility will do this nicely For examples the four images I just inlined here with links to their much larger originals have been pre scaled to pixels width by interposing thumbnails zooniverse org 300x into the URLs The whole shebang looks like this in the markdown input no line breaks no spaces except in the alt texts all in one single long line ! 4s around Q https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/730/3493090/ fuzzy range https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3494152/

test mass symmetrically aimed above and below the midpoint These beams are modulated with among other things a Hz sine wave The extra light pressure from a mere watts of near infrared light suffices "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN There's such a wide variety of glitches that a single way of turning them into images would not suffice Some are very tall and slender of short duration but spanning a broad band of frequencies Others are the opposite of long duration but limited to a few frequencies or just one Some are in between Our image production tries not always successfully to adapt to the shape of the glitch One and the same glitch can end up looking quite different depending on how it has been processed ! 4s around Q See also a list of Examples of common glitches at uncommon Q values tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk in our Talk pages snap > linking to the thread Apropos of this Any large size images inlined in the Field Guide should be pre scaled down from their original sizes to avoid having to load a half Megabyte image file only for the browser having to scale it down The thumbnail zooniverse org facility will do this nicely For examples the four images I just inlined here with links to their much larger originals have been pre scaled to pixels width by interposing thumbnails zooniverse org 300x into the URLs The whole shebang looks like this in the markdown input no line breaks no spaces except in the alt texts all in one single long line ! 4s around Q https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/730/3493090/ fuzzy range https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3494152/

Well obviously it did happen more examples of this kind will be welcome This is part of a subject set of glitches from Livingston that happened during the first months of the third observing run the present subject dates from the second day of O3a which had been processed and uploaded for use in Gravity Spy a year and a half ago but which have only now been associated with the active workflows So this is the very first example of its kind that we're getting to see The glitch in strain is a Crown a fast scattering glitch where the stray light was reflected by the edge of a large cylindrical baffle that was vibrating at a rate of several times per second modulated by slower pendulum motions one half period every couple of seconds of one of the test mass suspensions These glitches don't happen any more during the ongoing fourth observing run These cryopump baffles which had been vibration prone back then are better damped now The old glitch class proposal thread tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk includes a history of the mitigation efforts with links to some logbook entries with pictures The auxiliary channel represents the small amount of laser light that gets through the reflective mirror coating of Livingston's X end test mass and is picked up by a quadrant photodiode used in Alignment Sensing and Control ASC part of the machinery that keeps the beam spots in their proper places on all four test masses It's quite possible that the Crown glitches came from the Y end Since micro seismic ground motion happens at its own pace at each of the corner station and the two end stations several km away the motions of the test mass suspensions or better the motions of the vacuum chambers around each test mass and everything attached to the chamber walls are independent Seismic activity may be elevated in all three locations but any resulting glitches could well be interleaved like they are here "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them?
