First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN There's such a wide variety of glitches that a single way of turning them into images would not suffice Some are very tall and slender of short duration but spanning a broad band of frequencies Others are the opposite of long duration but limited to a few frequencies or just one Some are in between Our image production tries not always successfully to adapt to the shape of the glitch One and the same glitch can end up looking quite different depending on how it has been processed ! 4s around Q See also a list of Examples of common glitches at uncommon Q values tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk in our Talk pages snap > linking to the thread Apropos of this Any large size images inlined in the Field Guide should be pre scaled down from their original sizes to avoid having to load a half Megabyte image file only for the browser having to scale it down The thumbnail zooniverse org facility will do this nicely For examples the four images I just inlined here with links to their much larger originals have been pre scaled to pixels width by interposing thumbnails zooniverse org 300x into the URLs The whole shebang looks like this in the markdown input no line breaks no spaces except in the alt texts all in one single long line ! 4s around Q https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/730/3493090/ fuzzy range https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3494152/

"None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN There's such a wide variety of glitches that a single way of turning them into images would not suffice Some are very tall and slender of short duration but spanning a broad band of frequencies Others are the opposite of long duration but limited to a few frequencies or just one Some are in between Our image production tries not always successfully to adapt to the shape of the glitch One and the same glitch can end up looking quite different depending on how it has been processed ! 4s around Q See also a list of Examples of common glitches at uncommon Q values tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk in our Talk pages snap > linking to the thread Apropos of this Any large size images inlined in the Field Guide should be pre scaled down from their original sizes to avoid having to load a half Megabyte image file only for the browser having to scale it down The thumbnail zooniverse org facility will do this nicely For examples the four images I just inlined here with links to their much larger originals have been pre scaled to pixels width by interposing thumbnails zooniverse org 300x into the URLs The whole shebang looks like this in the markdown input no line breaks no spaces except in the alt texts all in one single long line ! 4s around Q https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/730/3493090/ fuzzy range https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3494152/

test mass symmetrically aimed above and below the midpoint These beams are modulated with among other things a Hz sine wave The extra light pressure from a mere watts of near infrared light suffices "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN There's such a wide variety of glitches that a single way of turning them into images would not suffice Some are very tall and slender of short duration but spanning a broad band of frequencies Others are the opposite of long duration but limited to a few frequencies or just one Some are in between Our image production tries not always successfully to adapt to the shape of the glitch One and the same glitch can end up looking quite different depending on how it has been processed ! 4s around Q See also a list of Examples of common glitches at uncommon Q values tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk in our Talk pages snap > linking to the thread Apropos of this Any large size images inlined in the Field Guide should be pre scaled down from their original sizes to avoid having to load a half Megabyte image file only for the browser having to scale it down The thumbnail zooniverse org facility will do this nicely For examples the four images I just inlined here with links to their much larger originals have been pre scaled to pixels width by interposing thumbnails zooniverse org 300x into the URLs The whole shebang looks like this in the markdown input no line breaks no spaces except in the alt texts all in one single long line ! 4s around Q https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/730/3493090/ fuzzy range https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3494152/

Well obviously it did happen more examples of this kind will be welcome This is part of a subject set of glitches from Livingston that happened during the first months of the third observing run the present subject dates from the second day of O3a which had been processed and uploaded for use in Gravity Spy a year and a half ago but which have only now been associated with the active workflows So this is the very first example of its kind that we're getting to see The glitch in strain is a Crown a fast scattering glitch where the stray light was reflected by the edge of a large cylindrical baffle that was vibrating at a rate of several times per second modulated by slower pendulum motions one half period every couple of seconds of one of the test mass suspensions These glitches don't happen any more during the ongoing fourth observing run These cryopump baffles which had been vibration prone back then are better damped now The old glitch class proposal thread tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk includes a history of the mitigation efforts with links to some logbook entries with pictures The auxiliary channel represents the small amount of laser light that gets through the reflective mirror coating of Livingston's X end test mass and is picked up by a quadrant photodiode used in Alignment Sensing and Control ASC part of the machinery that keeps the beam spots in their proper places on all four test masses It's quite possible that the Crown glitches came from the Y end Since micro seismic ground motion happens at its own pace at each of the corner station and the two end stations several km away the motions of the test mass suspensions or better the motions of the vacuum chambers around each test mass and everything attached to the chamber walls are independent Seismic activity may be elevated in all three locations but any resulting glitches could well be interleaved like they are here "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN There's such a wide variety of glitches that a single way of turning them into images would not suffice Some are very tall and slender of short duration but spanning a broad band of frequencies Others are the opposite of long duration but limited to a few frequencies or just one Some are in between Our image production tries not always successfully to adapt to the shape of the glitch One and the same glitch can end up looking quite different depending on how it has been processed ! 4s around Q See also a list of Examples of common glitches at uncommon Q values tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk in our Talk pages snap > linking to the thread Apropos of this Any large size images inlined in the Field Guide should be pre scaled down from their original sizes to avoid having to load a half Megabyte image file only for the browser having to scale it down The thumbnail zooniverse org facility will do this nicely For examples the four images I just inlined here with links to their much larger originals have been pre scaled to pixels width by interposing thumbnails zooniverse org 300x into the URLs The whole shebang looks like this in the markdown input no line breaks no spaces except in the alt texts all in one single long line ! 4s around Q https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/730/3493090/ fuzzy range https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3494152/

"None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN There's such a wide variety of glitches that a single way of turning them into images would not suffice Some are very tall and slender of short duration but spanning a broad band of frequencies Others are the opposite of long duration but limited to a few frequencies or just one Some are in between Our image production tries not always successfully to adapt to the shape of the glitch One and the same glitch can end up looking quite different depending on how it has been processed ! 4s around Q See also a list of Examples of common glitches at uncommon Q values tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk in our Talk pages snap > linking to the thread Apropos of this Any large size images inlined in the Field Guide should be pre scaled down from their original sizes to avoid having to load a half Megabyte image file only for the browser having to scale it down The thumbnail zooniverse org facility will do this nicely For examples the four images I just inlined here with links to their much larger originals have been pre scaled to pixels width by interposing thumbnails zooniverse org 300x into the URLs The whole shebang looks like this in the markdown input no line breaks no spaces except in the alt texts all in one single long line ! 4s around Q https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/730/3493090/ fuzzy range https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3494152/

LLO Images from the LIGO logbooks courtesy Caltech MIT LIGO Laboratory tab A brief disturbance of the RF modulation amplitude would show up after demodulation as a spike in several photodiode channels The Length Sensing and Control LSC subsystem might mistake it for a disturbance in the distance between a pair of mirrors and would react by sending signals to the mirror suspensions to "correct" the perceived excursion only to introduce an excursion which then needs to be counteracted during the following tens of milliseconds Similarly the Alignment Sensing and Control ASC subystem might misinterpret such a spike as a mirror or two having turned away from their correct angles and would send a "correction" to the suspensions which afterwards would need to be countermanded These coupling paths are what can give rise to a compound glitch shape in our Gravity Spy images a very brief broadband blip followed by low frequency rumbles during the momentary length and alignment excursions The LSC and ASC control loops have been reworked and refined many times over the years their reactions nowadays would be more subtle The initial blip would often also show up in an auxiliary channel dedicated to monitoring the RF modulation amplitude LSC MOD RF AM CTRL OUT DQ Other kinds of RF malfunctions giving rise to other glitch shapes in our image would also stand a good chance of being witnessed by this channel The original series Hanford September Already during Engineering Run before the first Observing Run of Advanced LIGO there had been occurrences of this kind of glitch and some effort had been made to locate the cause A few days into O from Sunday onwards another spate of these glitches began to plague the Hanford interferometer The linked subject above was among the earliest of these Showing the third frames of some examples ! It turns out that when the Gravity Spy Machine Learning was trained on genuine examples it settled on the shapes of the individual glitchlets without any regard to their periodicity and alternation on their "Dove" aspect without regard to the "Paired" trait Thousands of later glitches of unrelated types have thus ended up with inappropriate Paired Doves labels Background LHO tab Paired Doves glitches were happening while a number of mirrors on the output side of the interferometer were developing oscillations in pitch tipping up and down around a horizontal axis that started gently and gradually got worse over the course of a few minutes each time ending in a lockloss The ultimate cause was never conclusively determined it could have been an instability in the angular control of the Beam Splitter at Hz close to a mechanical resonance of the BS suspension or the BS angular control could itself have been reacting to something else Every actively controlled mirror "downstream" from the BS along the output path was tipping at the same pace trying to track the faint output beam through its vertical wobbles Once the motion had got large enough a glitchlet "dove" appeared whenever the wobbling beam was at the highest or at the lowest point of its excursions Here is a view of Hanford's central Beam Splitter as it looked prior to O from LHO tab ! "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN The Glitch Paleontological Museum Over the last nine years writing in late Advanced LIGO has come a long way The interferometers and the glitch mix coming out of them! have changed faster than the Gravity Spy glitch class notions Updating the Gravity Spy Machine Learning to accommodate new glitch classes is hard and tedious work tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 3369772?comment Some glitch classes from earlier observing runs have gone the way of the trilobites they're well and truly extinct now We've been keeping them around for didactic purposes Some have gone the way of the dinoasaurs their descendants are still among us but they look very different nowadays and no longer resemble their fossil ancestors very much so we now call them "birds" bird Some have gone the way of the Coealacanths They were thought to have gone extinct but seem to have returned tab Or else an entirely different glitch cause may now be at work originating from some component that didn't even exist yet during past observing runs producing false friends lookalike glitches that have re occupied a vacant ecological niche Or a surviving old population of glitches may now be sharing its habitat with a new one of different origin but looking confusingly similar There are fish in the oceans and then there are dolphins too Lookalikes can confuse the Machine Learning and us human volunteers alike In both cases the result is mission creep New phenomena get mistakenly subsumed under old glitch classes where they don't belong Our human brains tend to be biased towards the familiar it takes more of a mental effort to identify something as an unfamiliar "None Of The Above" than to shoehorn it into a known class even though it doesn't belong And the Machine Learning nowadays doesn't even have a way of signalling "None Of The Above" it will label each and every subjects with one of the glitch classes it has been trained for A low estimated confidence would be the only hint that the subject didn't in fact fit anywhere among the classes known to the ML Combining the data release tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2583278?comment with a deep dive into old logbook entries https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/6706/3502533/ Extinct glitch classes living fossils tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk O and O Light Modulation Status Known from Hanford during O and O Doubtful very rare if present from Livingston during O Not seen during O or O so far believed extinct This is a glitch class which has been named for the subsystem in which the cause had resided but described and defined by its visual appearance It turns out that other kinds of malfunctions in the same subsystem later caused quite a variety of glitches that look totally different some that were given other names some remaining nameless There exist glitches coming from the laser light modulation machinery which do not at all resemble the Light Modulation class for which the Gravity Spy Machine Learning has been trained and which is described in our Field Guide Conversely glitch shapes which somewhat resemble the original Light Modulation glitches compound shapes which look like a blip followed by low frequency noise can arise in other ways from causes that have nothing to do with the light modulation machinery False friends As a results hundreds of O subjects and at least dozens of O subjects have got mis labeled as Light Modulation by the ML Background The main near infrared nm laser beam gets phase modulated with several short wave radio frequencies including MHz and MHz often abbreviated "RF9" and "RF45" in order to create sidebands some amount of laser light of very slightly shorter and longer wavelengths which unlike the carrier light won't resonate between the test mass mirrors in the arms The sidebands confined to the central interferometer can then be used as a reference against which we can measure tab There are quite a few components involved in creating and applying the radio frequency signals and thus quite a few places where something could sometimes go wrong all of which would need to be investigated by the LIGO engineers during glitch hunting There's a reference oscillator running at MHz LHO tab ! LHO EOM in its surroundings ! LHO EOM connections Some of the equipment including some of the RF cables in the electronics room just to give an impression ! LLO Images from the LIGO logbooks courtesy Caltech MIT LIGO Laboratory tab A brief disturbance of the RF modulation amplitude would show up after demodulation as a spike in several photodiode channels The Length Sensing and Control LSC subsystem might mistake it for a disturbance in the distance between a pair of mirrors and would react by sending signals to the mirror suspensions to "correct" the perceived excursion only to introduce an excursion which then needs to be counteracted during the following tens of milliseconds Similarly the Alignment Sensing and Control ASC subystem might misinterpret such a spike as a mirror or two having turned away from their correct angles and would send a "correction" to the suspensions which afterwards would need to be countermanded These coupling paths are what can give rise to a compound glitch shape in our Gravity Spy images a very brief broadband blip followed by low frequency rumbles during the momentary length and alignment excursions The LSC and ASC control loops have been reworked and refined many times over the years their reactions nowadays would be more subtle The initial blip would often also show up in an auxiliary channel dedicated to monitoring the RF modulation amplitude LSC MOD RF AM CTRL OUT DQ Other kinds of RF malfunctions giving rise to other glitch shapes in our image would also stand a good chance of being witnessed by this channel The original series Hanford September Already during Engineering Run before the first Observing Run of Advanced LIGO there had been occurrences of this kind of glitch and some effort had been made to locate the cause A few days into O from Sunday onwards another spate of these glitches began to plague the Hanford interferometer The linked subject above was among the earliest of these Showing the third frames of some examples ! "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN baffle that was vibrating at a rate of several times per second modulated by slower pendulum motions one half period every couple of seconds of one of the test mass suspensions These glitches don't happen any more during the ongoing fourth observing run These cryopump baffles which had been vibration prone back then are better damped now The old glitch class proposal thread tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk includes a history of the mitigation efforts with links to some logbook entries with pictures The auxiliary channel represents the small amount of laser light that gets through the reflective mirror coating of Livingston's X end test mass and is picked up by a quadrant photodiode used in Alignment Sensing and Control ASC part of the machinery that keeps the beam spots in their proper places on all four test masses It's quite possible that the Crown glitches came from the Y end Since micro seismic ground motion happens at its own pace at each of the corner station and the two end stations several km away the motions of the test mass suspensions or better the motions of the vacuum chambers around each test mass and everything attached to the chamber walls are independent Seismic activity may be elevated in all three locations but any resulting glitches could well be interleaved like they are here The Glitch Paleontological Museum Over the last nine years writing in late Advanced LIGO has come a long way The interferometers and the glitch mix coming out of them! have changed faster than the Gravity Spy glitch class notions Updating the Gravity Spy Machine Learning to accommodate new glitch classes is hard and tedious work tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 3369772?comment Some glitch classes from earlier observing runs have gone the way of the trilobites they're well and truly extinct now We've been keeping them around for didactic purposes Some have gone the way of the dinoasaurs their descendants are still among us but they look very different nowadays and no longer resemble their fossil ancestors very much so we now call them "birds" bird Some have gone the way of the Coealacanths They were thought to have gone extinct but seem to have returned tab Or else an entirely different glitch cause may now be at work originating from some component that didn't even exist yet during past observing runs producing false friends lookalike glitches that have re occupied a vacant ecological niche Or a surviving old population of glitches may now be sharing its habitat with a new one of different origin but looking confusingly similar There are fish in the oceans and then there are dolphins too Lookalikes can confuse the Machine Learning and us human volunteers alike In both cases the result is mission creep New phenomena get mistakenly subsumed under old glitch classes where they don't belong Our human brains tend to be biased towards the familiar it takes more of a mental effort to identify something as an unfamiliar "None Of The Above" than to shoehorn it into a known class even though it doesn't belong And the Machine Learning nowadays doesn't even have a way of signalling "None Of The Above" it will label each and every subjects with one of the glitch classes it has been trained for A low estimated confidence would be the only hint that the subject didn't in fact fit anywhere among the classes known to the ML Combining the data release tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2583278?comment with a deep dive into old logbook entries yields some insights and a few surprises to me at any rate Shovels ready? Prepared to get your fingers dirty? https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/6706/3502533/ Extinct glitch classes living fossils tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk O and O Light Modulation Status Known from Hanford during O and O Doubtful very rare if present from Livingston during O Not seen during O or O so far believed extinct This is a glitch class which has been named for the subsystem in which the cause had resided but described and defined by its visual appearance It turns out that other kinds of malfunctions in the same subsystem later caused quite a variety of glitches that look totally different some that were given other names some remaining nameless There exist glitches coming from the laser light modulation machinery which do not at all resemble the Light Modulation class for which the Gravity Spy Machine Learning has been trained and which is described in our Field Guide Conversely glitch shapes which somewhat resemble the original Light Modulation glitches compound shapes which look like a blip followed by low frequency noise can arise in other ways from causes that have nothing to do with the light modulation machinery False friends As a results hundreds of O subjects and at least dozens of O subjects have got mis labeled as Light Modulation by the ML Background The main near infrared nm laser beam gets phase modulated with several short wave radio frequencies including MHz and MHz often abbreviated "RF9" and "RF45" in order to create sidebands some amount of laser light of very slightly shorter and longer wavelengths which unlike the carrier light won't resonate between the test mass mirrors in the arms The sidebands confined to the central interferometer can then be used as a reference against which we can measure tab There are quite a few components involved in creating and applying the radio frequency signals and thus quite a few places where something could sometimes go wrong all of which would need to be investigated by the LIGO      Interesting catch! Well obviously it did happen more examples of this kind will be welcome This is part of a subject set of glitches from Livingston that happened during the first months of the third observing run the present subject dates from the second day of O3a which had been processed and uploaded for use in Gravity Spy a year and a half ago but which have only now been associated with the active workflows So this is the very first example of its kind that we're getting to see The glitch in strain is a Crown a fast scattering glitch where the stray light was reflected by the edge of a large cylindrical baffle that was vibrating at a rate of several times per second modulated by slower pendulum motions one half period every couple of seconds of one of the test mass suspensions These glitches don't happen any more during the ongoing fourth observing run These cryopump baffles which had been vibration prone back then are better damped now The old glitch class proposal thread tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk includes a history of the mitigation efforts with links to some logbook entries with pictures The auxiliary channel represents the small amount of laser light that gets through the reflective mirror coating of Livingston's X end test mass and is picked up by a quadrant photodiode used in Alignment Sensing and Control ASC part of the machinery that keeps the beam spots in their proper places on all four test masses It's quite possible that the Crown glitches came from the Y end Since micro seismic ground motion happens at its own pace at each of the corner station and the two end stations several km away the motions of the test mass suspensions or better the motions of the vacuum chambers around each test mass and everything attached to the chamber walls are independent Seismic activity may be elevated in all three locations but any resulting glitches could well be interleaved like they are here The Glitch Paleontological Museum Over the last nine years writing in late Advanced LIGO has come a long way The interferometers and the glitch mix coming out of them! have changed faster than the Gravity Spy glitch class notions Updating the Gravity Spy Machine Learning to accommodate new glitch classes is hard and tedious work tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 3369772?comment Some glitch classes from earlier observing runs have gone the way of the trilobites they're well and truly extinct now We've been keeping them around for didactic purposes Some have gone the way of the dinoasaurs their descendants are still among us but they look very different nowadays and no longer resemble their fossil ancestors very much so we now call them "birds" bird Some have gone the way of the Coealacanths They were thought to have gone extinct but seem to have returned tab Or else an entirely different glitch cause may now be at work originating from some component that didn't even exist yet during past observing runs producing false friends lookalike glitches that have re occupied a vacant ecological niche Or a surviving old population of glitches may now be sharing its habitat with a new one of different origin but looking confusingly similar There are fish in the oceans and then there are dolphins too Lookalikes can confuse the Machine Learning and us human volunteers alike In both cases the result is mission creep New phenomena get mistakenly subsumed under old glitch classes where they don't belong Our human brains tend to be biased towards the familiar it takes more of a mental effort to identify something as an unfamiliar "None Of The Above" than to shoehorn it into a known class even though it doesn't belong And the Machine Learning nowadays doesn't even have a way of signalling "None Of The Above" it will label each and every subjects with one of the glitch classes it has been trained for A low estimated confidence would be the only hint that the subject didn't in fact fit anywhere among the classes known to the ML Combining the data release tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2583278?comment with a deep dive into old logbook entries      Interesting catch! Well obviously it did happen more examples of this kind will be welcome This is part of a subject set of glitches from Livingston that happened during the first months of the third observing run the present subject dates from the second day of O3a which had been processed and uploaded for use in Gravity Spy a year and a half ago but which have only now been associated with the active workflows So this is the very first example of its kind that we're getting to see The glitch in strain is a Crown a fast scattering glitch where the stray light was reflected by the edge of a large cylindrical baffle that was vibrating at a rate of several times per second modulated by slower pendulum motions one half period every couple of seconds of one of the test mass suspensions These glitches don't happen any more during the ongoing fourth observing run These cryopump baffles which had been vibration prone back then are better damped now The old glitch class proposal thread tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk includes a history of the mitigation efforts with links to some logbook entries with pictures The auxiliary channel represents the small amount of laser light that gets through the reflective mirror coating of Livingston's X end test mass and is picked up by a quadrant photodiode used in Alignment Sensing and Control ASC part of the machinery that keeps the beam spots in their proper places on all four test masses It's quite possible that the Crown glitches came from the Y end Since micro seismic ground motion happens at its own pace at each of the corner station and the two end stations several km away the motions of the test mass suspensions or better the motions of the vacuum chambers around each test mass and everything attached to the chamber walls are independent Seismic activity may be elevated in all three locations but any resulting glitches could well be interleaved like they are here Gravity Spy glitch class notions Updating the Gravity Spy Machine Learning to accommodate new glitch classes is hard and tedious work tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 3369772?comment Some glitch classes from earlier observing runs have gone the way of the trilobites they're well and truly extinct now We've been keeping them around for didactic purposes Some have gone the way of the dinoasaurs their descendants are still among us but they look very different nowadays and no longer resemble their fossil ancestors very much so we now call them "birds" bird Some have gone the way of the Coealacanths They were thought to have gone extinct but seem to have returned tab Or else an entirely different glitch cause may now be at work originating from some component that didn't even exist yet during past observing runs producing false friends lookalike glitches that have re occupied a vacant ecological niche Or a surviving old population of glitches may now be sharing its habitat with a new one of different origin but looking confusingly similar There are fish in the oceans and then there are dolphins too Lookalikes can confuse the Machine Learning and us human volunteers alike In both cases the result is mission creep New phenomena get mistakenly subsumed under old glitch classes where they don't belong Our human brains tend to be biased towards the familiar it takes more of a mental effort to identify something as an unfamiliar "None Of The Above" than to shoehorn it into a known class even though it doesn't belong And the Machine Learning nowadays doesn't even have a way of signalling "None Of The Above" it will label each and every subjects with one of the glitch classes it has been trained for A low estimated confidence would be the only hint that the LLO Images from the LIGO logbooks courtesy Caltech MIT LIGO Laboratory tab A brief disturbance of the RF modulation amplitude would show up after demodulation as a spike in several photodiode channels The Length Sensing and Control LSC subsystem might mistake it for a disturbance in the distance between a pair of mirrors and would react by sending signals to the mirror suspensions to "correct" the perceived excursion only to introduce an excursion which then needs to be counteracted during the following tens of milliseconds Similarly the Alignment Sensing and Control ASC subystem might misinterpret such a spike as a mirror or two having turned away from their correct angles and would send a "correction" to the suspensions which afterwards would need to be countermanded These coupling paths are what can give rise to a compound glitch shape in our Gravity Spy images a very brief broadband blip followed by low frequency rumbles during the momentary length and alignment excursions The LSC and ASC control loops have been reworked and refined many times over the years their reactions nowadays would be more subtle The initial blip would often also show up in an auxiliary channel dedicated to monitoring the RF modulation amplitude LSC MOD RF AM CTRL OUT DQ Other kinds of RF malfunctions giving rise to other glitch shapes in our image would also stand a good chance of being witnessed by this channel The original series Hanford September Already during Engineering Run before the first Observing Run of Advanced LIGO there had been occurrences of this kind of glitch and some effort had been made to locate the cause A few days into O from Sunday onwards another spate of these glitches began to plague the Hanford interferometer The linked subject above was among the earliest of these Showing the third frames of some examples ! It turns out that when the Gravity Spy Machine Learning was trained on genuine examples it settled on the shapes of the individual glitchlets without any regard to their periodicity and alternation on their "Dove" aspect without regard to the "Paired" trait Thousands of later glitches of unrelated types have thus ended up with inappropriate Paired Doves labels Background LHO tab Paired Doves glitches were happening while a number of mirrors on the output side of the interferometer were developing oscillations in pitch tipping up and down around a horizontal axis that started gently and gradually got worse over the course of a few minutes each time ending in a lockloss The ultimate cause was never conclusively determined it could have been an instability in the angular control of the Beam Splitter at Hz close to a mechanical resonance of the BS suspension or the BS angular control could itself have been reacting to something else Every actively controlled mirror "downstream" from the BS along the output path was tipping at the same pace trying to track the faint output beam through its vertical wobbles Once the motion had got large enough a glitchlet "dove" appeared whenever the wobbling beam was at the highest or at the lowest point of its excursions Here is a view of Hanford's central Beam Splitter as it looked prior to O from LHO tab ! "None Of The Above" is always an option when something doesn't seem to fit into the available classes and it ensures that more people are going to get a look The "Repeating Blips" class available from the level workflow onwards was originally introduced to capture rows of blips that are all more or less the same size and shape and occupy the same frequency range where some cause was at work repeatedly up to several times per second and each time it happened it produced one single blip It could also happen that two blips of similar or different sizes and shapes appear together in the same subject image by mere coincidence But after "Repeating Blips" had been introduced we've also encountered other groups of multiple blips of which the present subject is a good example where a few blip like glitches of different sizes appear in a fairly tight group with irregular spacing along the time axis and with a definite beginning and end within the four seconds we get to see These have got nicknamed "flocks" and they appear to be a genuine seeparate glitch class of their own which has yet to be formally proposed Here it appears that a single cause is at work just once but couples into the gravitational strain channel through two or three distinct causal connections producing the entire group when it happens There's some prior discussion of these g here tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk If you see more of these why not start a collection of them? First of all it doesn't contain valid data near Hz where the loud glitch in strain appears tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2961842?comment so there's no way it could directly witness this glitch up there The same applies to H ASC REFL B RF Q YAW OUT DQ and H LSC POP A LF OUT DQ in tab and tab Second it does however have some noise at lower frequencies which starts and ends at the right moments Third there's loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz surrounded by spikes which suddenly stops around the time of the glitch and a dark whitening artefact band afterwards Fourth there's less loud narrowband noise somewhere around Hz which suddenly starts around the time of the glitch and a dark artefact band at this frequency before this point So what could possibly show up at a fairly high frequency in the strain channel on the output side of the interferometer and in a REFL channel on the input side even before the Power Recycling Cavity !? Noting that the PRC length could not easily produce fluctuations this fast in the arm cavities and that the alignment sensing and control loops are far slower Which leaves laser frequency noise that's normally controlled by a fast multi level feedback loop acting back on the PreStabilized Laser and locking it against the common arm length CARM so as to keep CARM at a constant multiple of the instantaneous laser wavelength And these glitches only happened between and Armed with this knowledge we head to the LHO logbook and find LHO tab The Hanford team aiming to improve noise levels at frequencies of several kHz had been experimenting from onwards with a higher gain of the CARM feedback loop On this change was reverted upon noticing that it had not helped as intended and that it had resulted in worse noise levels at some frequencies during the first two hours of each lock while the optics were gradually approaching thermal equilibrium It was also noticed that at this higher gain setting after each lock reacquisition some 1h 40m actually between one hour and two hours after reaching Nominal Low Noise and independently of when Observing resumed something changed state quite rapidly causing noise components near and kHz to disappear and noise near kHz to appear instead It turns out that our glitches happened during these state changes and that within each lock segment several of them could happen in succession before the changed state settled down All fourty five known glitches of this kind happened between one hour and two hours after reaching NLN from comparing the approximate timestamps to which we currently have access to the Detector Status Summary Pages from tab It also becomes clear why none of these glitches happened on because LHO kept observing and didn't lose lock until the evening and didn't resume Observing allowing glitches to be recorded after a UTC lock reacquisition until UTC the next day this time more than two hours after reaching NLN The Glitch Paleontological Museum Over the last nine years writing in late Advanced LIGO has come a long way The interferometers and the glitch mix coming out of them! have changed faster than the Gravity Spy glitch class notions Updating the Gravity Spy Machine Learning to accommodate new glitch classes is hard and tedious work tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 3369772?comment Some glitch classes from earlier observing runs have gone the way of the trilobites they're well and truly extinct now We've been keeping them around for didactic purposes Some have gone the way of the dinoasaurs their descendants are still among us but they look very different nowadays and no longer resemble their fossil ancestors very much so we now call them "birds" bird Some have gone the way of the Coealacanths They were thought to have gone extinct but seem to have returned tab Or else an entirely different glitch cause may now be at work originating from some component that didn't even exist yet during past observing runs producing false friends lookalike glitches that have re occupied a vacant ecological niche Or a surviving old population of glitches may now be sharing its habitat with a new one of different origin but looking confusingly similar There are fish in the oceans and then there are dolphins too Lookalikes can confuse the Machine Learning and us human volunteers alike In both cases the result is mission creep New phenomena get mistakenly subsumed under old glitch classes where they don't belong Our human brains tend to be biased towards the familiar it takes more of a mental effort to identify something as an unfamiliar "None Of The Above" than to shoehorn it into a known class even though it doesn't belong And the Machine Learning nowadays doesn't even have a way of signalling "None Of The Above" it will label each and every subjects with one of the glitch classes it has been trained for A low estimated confidence would be the only hint that the subject didn't in fact fit anywhere among the classes known to the ML Combining the data release tab projects zooniverse gravity spy talk 2583278?comment with a deep dive into old logbook entries
