But the reference to LLO tab But even that would only be of marginal interest to the Zooniverse Gravity Spy community For someone who would like a glimpse of how the Vacuum Team goes about troubleshooting such issues LLO tab It has also skipped LLO tab And MICH and SRCL aren't "sensors" As such they aren't channels either They are longitudinal degrees of freedom of the dual recycled interferometer and shorthands for feedback control loops which keep these degrees of freedom at their intended working points when the interferometer is locked The adjustments mentioned in LLO tab SRCL https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/6945/3780336 I have added this subject to my U shaped low frequency collection https www zooniverse org projects zooniverse gravity spy collections deleteduser shaped low frequency https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3780129 Filling in once again the missing proper searchable source citations and then some Re LHO tab Re LHO tab Conceptually what's going on is The interferometer sensing and control needs to know at any given moment as accurately as possible where each of the steerable optics is located and how it is oriented in order to drive the steering actuators to keep it in the desired place and orientation But it can't directly "see" where each mirror is! What it can work with are inputs from the optical sensors in the suspension actuators the "OS" bits of the OSEMs which provide an approximate and somewhat noisy measure of where each suspension stage is relative to the adjacent stages and inputs from the GS geophones in the Internal Seismic Isolations which sense the non inertial motions of the ISI stages and information about where the laser beam is from quadrant photodiodes and wavefront sensors The whereabouts of the optics must then be inferred from all this indirect evidence by a fairly involved computation in realtime too! Moreover both the ISI stages and the suspension stages have mechanical resonances at several low frequencies and any attempt to drive them near one of their resonances is likely to result in much larger motions than driving them at other frequencies The point of the new estimator control scheme then is to combine the data from the OSEMs and the GS13s in a novel way paying careful attention to which of the inputs is more accurate at which frequencies and using carefully tuned notch filters to make sure all the resonances are well damped while still being able to drive the suspensions at all other frequencies with sufficient authority to counteract any external ground motion coupled into them through the ISIs Such conceptual explanations are usually found in engineering documents and only rarely do they make it into the logbooks Here's a longer still selective! list of some of the relevant logbook entries from this month of August highlighting those which mention some of the conceptual ideas in bold LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab There's another subtle point here that none of these logbook entries make explicit because management level discussions that lead to policy decisions aren't logbook material we only see the consequences of these decisions reflected in the logs A considerable amount of time has been set aside for these commissioning activities although we're still in the middle of an observing run Why? But the reference to LLO tab But even that would only be of marginal interest to the Zooniverse Gravity Spy community For someone who would like a glimpse of how the Vacuum Team goes about troubleshooting such issues LLO tab It has also skipped LLO tab And MICH and SRCL aren't "sensors" As such they aren't channels either They are longitudinal degrees of freedom of the dual recycled interferometer and shorthands for feedback control loops which keep these degrees of freedom at their intended working points when the interferometer is locked The adjustments mentioned in LLO tab SRCL https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/6945/3780336 I have added this subject to my U shaped low frequency collection https www zooniverse org projects zooniverse gravity spy collections deleteduser shaped low frequency https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3780129 Filling in once again the missing proper searchable source citations and then some Re LHO tab Re LHO tab Conceptually what's going on is The interferometer sensing and control needs to know at any given moment as accurately as possible where each of the steerable optics is located and how it is oriented in order to drive the steering actuators to keep it in the desired place and orientation But it can't directly "see" where each mirror is! What it can work with are inputs from the optical sensors in the suspension actuators the "OS" bits of the OSEMs which provide an approximate and somewhat noisy measure of where each suspension stage is relative to the adjacent stages and inputs from the GS geophones in the Internal Seismic Isolations which sense the non inertial motions of the ISI stages and information about where the laser beam is from quadrant photodiodes and wavefront sensors The whereabouts of the optics must then be inferred from all this indirect evidence by a fairly involved computation in realtime too! Moreover both the ISI stages and the suspension stages have mechanical resonances at several low frequencies and any attempt to drive them near one of their resonances is likely to result in much larger motions than driving them at other frequencies The point of the new estimator control scheme then is to combine the data from the OSEMs and the GS13s in a novel way paying careful attention to which of the inputs is more accurate at which frequencies and using carefully tuned notch filters to make sure all the resonances are well damped while still being able to drive the suspensions at all other frequencies with sufficient authority to counteract any external ground motion coupled into them through the ISIs Such conceptual explanations are usually found in engineering documents and only rarely do they make it into the logbooks Here's a longer still selective! list of some of the relevant logbook entries from this month of August highlighting those which mention some of the conceptual ideas in bold LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab There's another subtle point here that none of these logbook entries make explicit because management level discussions that lead to policy decisions aren't logbook material we only see the consequences of these decisions reflected in the logs A considerable amount of time has been set aside for these commissioning activities although we're still in the middle of an observing run Why? But the reference to LLO tab But even that would only be of marginal interest to the Zooniverse Gravity Spy community For someone who would like a glimpse of how the Vacuum Team goes about troubleshooting such issues LLO tab It has also skipped LLO tab And MICH and SRCL aren't "sensors" As such they aren't channels either They are longitudinal degrees of freedom of the dual recycled interferometer and shorthands for feedback control loops which keep these degrees of freedom at their intended working points when the interferometer is locked The adjustments mentioned in LLO tab SRCL https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/6945/3780336 I have added this subject to my U shaped low frequency collection https www zooniverse org projects zooniverse gravity spy collections deleteduser shaped low frequency https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/zooniverse/gravity-spy/talk/328/3780129 Filling in once again the missing proper searchable source citations and then some Re LHO tab Re LHO tab Conceptually what's going on is The interferometer sensing and control needs to know at any given moment as accurately as possible where each of the steerable optics is located and how it is oriented in order to drive the steering actuators to keep it in the desired place and orientation But it can't directly "see" where each mirror is! What it can work with are inputs from the optical sensors in the suspension actuators the "OS" bits of the OSEMs which provide an approximate and somewhat noisy measure of where each suspension stage is relative to the adjacent stages and inputs from the GS geophones in the Internal Seismic Isolations which sense the non inertial motions of the ISI stages and information about where the laser beam is from quadrant photodiodes and wavefront sensors The whereabouts of the optics must then be inferred from all this indirect evidence by a fairly involved computation in realtime too! Moreover both the ISI stages and the suspension stages have mechanical resonances at several low frequencies and any attempt to drive them near one of their resonances is likely to result in much larger motions than driving them at other frequencies The point of the new estimator control scheme then is to combine the data from the OSEMs and the GS13s in a novel way paying careful attention to which of the inputs is more accurate at which frequencies and using carefully tuned notch filters to make sure all the resonances are well damped while still being able to drive the suspensions at all other frequencies with sufficient authority to counteract any external ground motion coupled into them through the ISIs Such conceptual explanations are usually found in engineering documents and only rarely do they make it into the logbooks Here's a longer still selective! list of some of the relevant logbook entries from this month of August highlighting those which mention some of the conceptual ideas in bold LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab There's another subtle point here that none of these logbook entries make explicit because management level discussions that lead to policy decisions aren't logbook material we only see the consequences of these decisions reflected in the logs A considerable amount of time has been set aside for these commissioning activities although we're still in the middle of an observing run Why? What it can work with are inputs from the optical sensors in the suspension actuators the "OS" bits of the OSEMs which provide an approximate and somewhat noisy measure of where each suspension stage is relative to the adjacent stages and inputs from the GS geophones in the Internal Seismic Isolations which sense the non inertial motions of the ISI stages and information about where the laser beam is from quadrant photodiodes and wavefront sensors The whereabouts of the optics must then be inferred from all this indirect evidence by a fairly involved computation in realtime too! Moreover both the ISI stages and the suspension stages have mechanical resonances at several low frequencies and any attempt to drive them near one of their resonances is likely to result in much larger motions than driving them at other frequencies The point of the new estimator control scheme then is to combine the data from the OSEMs and the GS13s in a novel way paying careful attention to which of the inputs is more accurate at which frequencies and using carefully tuned notch filters to make sure all the resonances are well damped while still being able to drive the suspensions at all other frequencies with sufficient authority to counteract any external ground motion coupled into them through the ISIs Such conceptual explanations are usually found in engineering documents and only rarely do they make it into the logbooks Here's a longer still selective! list of some of the relevant logbook entries from this month of August highlighting those which mention some of the conceptual ideas in bold LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab LHO tab There's another subtle point here that none of these logbook entries make explicit because management level discussions that lead to policy decisions aren't logbook material we only see the consequences of these decisions reflected in the logs A considerable amount of time has been set aside for these commissioning activities although we're still in the middle of an observing run Why?
